proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(d_n=h_{1,n}-h_{0,n}\) and
\[
e_{k,n}=\|\Pi_{n,k}d_n\|_n^2,
\qquad k=1,\ldots,M.
\]
The complete potential-outcome schedule is fixed throughout; every probability, covariance, and variance without the subscript \(n\) is taken only over the two-stage assignment in Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}.
Assumption~\ref{ass:bounded-potential-outcomes} and the definition of \(h_{z,n}\) imply
\[
|h_{z,n}(A)|
\leq \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i\in A}|Y_{i,n}(z,A)|
\leq B.                                                     \tag{1}
\]
Consequently,
\[
V_{z,n}
=\mathbb E_n\!\left[(h_{z,n}-\mathbb E_nh_{z,n})^2\right]
\leq \mathbb E_n[h_{z,n}^2]
\leq B^2.                                                   \tag{2}
\]
By the orthogonal decomposition in Definition~\ref{def:johnson-decomposition},
\[
\sum_{k=1}^M e_{k,n}
=\operatorname{Var}_n\{d_n(A)\}
\leq \mathbb E_n[d_n(A)^2]
\leq 4B^2.                                                  \tag{3}
\]
Since \(N_n=MG_n\leq n\), fixed \(M\), and \(G_n\to\infty\) by Assumption~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, we have \(n\to\infty\).  Thus it suffices to consider \(n\geq4M\).

Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} gives, for \(1\leq k\leq M\),
\[
|\lambda_{n,k}|
=\frac{(M)_k}{(n-M)_k}
=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{M-j}{n-M-j}.
\]
When \(n\geq4M\), each numerator is at most \(M\), and each denominator is at least \(n-2M+1\geq n/2\).  Hence
\[
|\lambda_{n,k}|\leq\left(\frac{2M}{n}\right)^k.            \tag{4}
\]
For the degrees \(k\geq2\), equations (3)--(4) and \(G_n=N_n/M\leq n/M\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|G_n\sum_{k=2}^M\lambda_{n,k}e_{k,n}\right|
&\leq G_n\left(\frac{2M}{n}\right)^2
       \sum_{k=2}^M e_{k,n}\\
&\leq \frac{n}{M}\frac{4M^2}{n^2}\,4B^2
=\frac{16MB^2}{n}.                                         \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves, uniformly over all schedules obeying Assumption~\ref{ass:bounded-potential-outcomes}, that the combined contribution of all Johnson degrees at least two is \(O(n^{-1})\) after multiplication by \(G_n\).

For degree one, Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} gives \(\lambda_{n,1}=-M/(n-M)\).  Combining this identity with (5) and \(e_{1,n}=E_{\tau,1,n}\) gives the sharper deterministic expansion
\[
G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}
=-\frac{MG_n}{n-M}e_{1,n}+O(n^{-1})
=-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}).                   \tag{6}
\]

The same argument controls the arm-specific disjoint covariances.  Indeed, orthogonality and (2) give
\[
C_{zz,n}
=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}
  \|\Pi_{n,k}h_{z,n}\|_n^2,
\qquad
\sum_{k=1}^M\|\Pi_{n,k}h_{z,n}\|_n^2=V_{z,n}\leq B^2.
\]
Because \(2M/n\leq1/2\), equation (4) implies \(|\lambda_{n,k}|\leq2M/n\) for every \(k\geq1\).  Therefore
\[
|C_{zz,n}|\leq\frac{2MB^2}{n}.                              \tag{7}
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction} supplies constants \(\delta>0\) and \(n_0\) such that \(p_n\geq\delta\) and \(1-p_n\geq\delta\) for \(n\geq n_0\).  Thus (7) implies
\[
\left|\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}+
       \frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}\right|
\leq\frac{4MB^2}{\delta n}=O(n^{-1}).                      \tag{8}
\]

Multiplying the exact identity in Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-pame-variance} by \(G_n\), and using \(G_{1n}=p_nG_n\) and \(G_{0n}=(1-p_n)G_n\), gives
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2
=R_n+G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}
 -\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}-\frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}.
\]
Substitution of (6) and (8) proves the schedule-uniform finite-density expansion
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2
=R_n-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}).                \tag{9}
\]
No scaled-variance lower bound has been used.

Assumption~\ref{ass:sampling-fraction} and fixed \(M\) imply
\[
\frac{N_n}{n-M}
=\frac{N_n/n}{1-M/n}\longrightarrow\rho.                  \tag{10}
\]
Moreover, (3) gives \(0\leq E_{\tau,1,n}\leq4B^2\).  It follows from (6) and (10) that
\[
G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}
=O(n^{-1})+
 \left(\rho-\frac{N_n}{n-M}\right)E_{\tau,1,n}
\longrightarrow0.                                         \tag{11}
\]
Equation (8) proves the second asserted vanishing relation, while (9)--(10) prove
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).
\]
Together with (5), these equations prove every assertion of the theorem using only group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, fixed \(M\), and bounded potential outcomes.

For the unconditional CR2 comparison used downstream, fix \(z\in\{0,1\}\), put \(m=G_{zn}\), and let \(f\) be either \(h_{z,n}\) or \(h_{z,n}^2\).  Under Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}, the groups selected into arm \(z\) are an exchangeable ordered disjoint \(m\)-tuple.  If \(f^\circ=f-\mathbb E_nf\), direct expansion of the variance of their average gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m f(A_j)\right\}
=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_n(f)}m
\frac{m-1}{m}\langle f^\circ,\mathsf K_nf^\circ\rangle_n. \tag{12}
\]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity}, orthogonality, and (4),
\[
\left|\langle f^\circ,\mathsf K_nf^\circ\rangle_n\right|
\leq\frac{2M}{n}\operatorname{Var}_n(f).                  \tag{13}
\]
Stable treatment fractions give \(m\asymp G_n\), so \(m\to\infty\) and \(m\geq2\) eventually; also \(G_n\leq n/M\).  Since (1) bounds both \(f=h_{z,n}\) and \(f=h_{z,n}^2\), equations (12)--(13) give a constant \(K<\infty\), independent of the schedule, such that
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left\{m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m f(A_j)\right\}
\leq\frac{K}{G_n}.                                         \tag{14}
\]
For every \(L>0\), the elementary inequality
\[
\mathbb E[X^2]\geq \frac{L^2}{G_n}
 \Pr\!\left\{|X|>\frac{L}{\sqrt{G_n}}\right\}
\]
applied to the centered empirical average and (14) proves an \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) error for both its first and second moments.  Since \(m/(m-1)=1+O(G_n^{-1})\), the sample-variance identity in Definition~\ref{def:cr2-statistic} therefore gives
\[
s_{z,n}^2-V_{z,n}=O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}).                \tag{15}
\]
Consequently,
\[
G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n
=O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}),                                \tag{16}
\]
and combining (9) with (16) yields the entirely unconditional comparison
\[
G_n\bigl(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2\bigr)
=\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}
 +O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}).                        \tag{17}
\]
Neither predictable quadratic-variation stabilization nor scaled-variance nondegeneracy is used in (12)--(17).  When \(N_n=o(n)\) and \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\), the deterministic term in (17) has order \(N_n/n\), whereas the proved stochastic remainder is bounded by order \(G_n^{-1/2}\asymp N_n^{-1/2}\).  These rates agree at \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\).  Because (15) is only an upper bound, this identifies a benchmark crossover and does not assert a matching stochastic lower bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every array satisfying group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, and bounded potential outcomes, \[G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).\] More precisely, \(G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\to0\) and \(C_{11,n}/p_n+C_{00,n}/(1-p_n)\to0\); all Johnson degrees \(k\ge2\) vanish at the \(G_n\)-scale uniformly over the bounded schedules.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Scaled-variance nondegeneracy is a downstream studentization condition, not a premise of the spectral expansion. Equations (1)--(11) prove the stated conclusion without it, so retaining it would misstate the theorem's primitive scope.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The condition is retained but classified explicitly as a filtration-side conditional premise. Pollard's theorem consumes this condition; bounded schedules do not establish it over the full class.

proposed.statement: For every array satisfying group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, and bounded potential outcomes, \[G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).\] More precisely, \(G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\to0\) and \(C_{11,n}/p_n+C_{00,n}/(1-p_n)\to0\); all Johnson degrees \(k\ge2\) vanish at the \(G_n\)-scale uniformly over the bounded schedules.
proposed.justification: The degree-one Johnson projection is the unique first-order memory of finite-pool competition, and the exact coefficient \(N_n/(n-M)\) yields a schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) remainder without a scaled-variance lower bound.
proposed.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} covers this design as the homogeneous \(K=1\) member of a fixed finite group-size menu and obtains inference through \(N_n^2/n\to0\) plus its Assumption 1. The present Kneser expansion is unconditional under bounded fixed-size schedules; only the subsequent Gaussian and coverage conclusions trade those comparator conditions for the separate predictable-QV premise.
proposed.consumer: The exact coefficient determines the correct standard-error comparison at positive density. The unconditional \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) fluctuation upper bound gives \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) as a benchmark crossover when \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\), without asserting a matching stochastic lower bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem's statement and dependency graph must remove the unused nondegeneracy premise. The random-partition and CR2 definitions are declared because the proof also establishes the unconditional downstream CR2 expansion and its fluctuation bound.

prose_updates.tldr: Randomly formed groups cease to behave as independent regression clusters when a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The exact normalized Kneser operator gives an unconditional finite-sample variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order; neither this expansion nor the CR2 variance comparison uses predictable-QV stabilization or scaled-variance nondegeneracy. Pointwise centered Gaussian inference and CR2 coverage are separate conditional conclusions for the named class that imposes predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation filtration, together with nondegeneracy; bounded schedules alone are not claimed to imply that premise. CR2 estimates the independent-group term, so at positive density it is asymptotically conservative and is ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible, conditional on the inference premises. When the sampling fraction vanishes, studentized normality holds without \(N_n^2/n\to0\), but this trades the comparator's Assumption 1 and birthday condition for the explicit filtration-side premise. The eight-unit witness has exact variance \(1/7\) and expected CR2 \(2/7\). Finally, the all-statistic variance-impossibility theorem holds already on the additive no-interference subclass and therefore transfers to arbitrary composition interference; its special Rademacher construction verifies predictable-QV stability separately and does not establish that property for every bounded schedule.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws under its Assumption 1 and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation discards first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while the fixed-cluster CR2 literature has no mechanism for restoring it. Bounded composition schedules by themselves also do not supply predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the exact reveal filtration.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so exact causal variance and the CR2 comparison can be decomposed unconditionally by Johnson degree before any Gaussian approximation is invoked. Inference is then layered on transparently for the named predictable-QV-stable class rather than presented as a consequence of boundedness.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance, the schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) dense expansion, and the unconditional CR2 fluctuation bound; proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale; and, under an explicitly separate filtration-side predictable-QV premise and scaled-variance nondegeneracy, derives a centered martingale CLT and Wald coverage. It also characterizes the CR2 sharpness frontier, verifies the versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) consumer and the finite witness, and proves an all-statistic exact-variance impossibility theorem using a construction-specific predictable-QV calculation and deterministic diagonal selection.

prose_updates.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 permits a fixed finite menu of group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 obtain asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive theory treats the exact homogeneous \(K=1\) structural subcase. Its exact Kneser variance and CR2 expansions are unconditional under the stated fixed-size design conditions, whereas its Gaussian and coverage conclusions replace the comparator's inference conditions by scaled-variance nondegeneracy and the explicit statistic-specific predictable-QV premise. This is an assumption trade, not a pure weakening, because predictable-QV stabilization is not derived for the full bounded-schedule class. Positive homogeneous conclusions are not claimed for variable group sizes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies the classical Kneser spectrum, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform complete randomization, while \cite{Pollard1984}, Theorem VIII.1, supplies the martingale-array implication after predictable variation and conditional Lindeberg have been established or imposed as stated. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) 0.7.0 and \({\tt sandwich}\) 3.1-3 source contracts supply the software assembly, default-target, adjustment, bread, and scale semantics used by the exact consumer proposition; \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explains CR2 calibration under independent-cluster working models, and \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. None supplies the random-partition projection correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; neither subsumes the proved equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound. That lower bound holds on an additive no-interference subclass and hence transfers to the full arbitrary-composition class. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias is \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization is a filtration-side conditional premise for the general CLT and coverage results, not a consequence proved from bounded schedules; its verification for the Rademacher lower-bound priors is construction-specific. The Rademacher variance limits are separated only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their gap vanishes. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation bound is only an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is a benchmark crossover rather than a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results are restricted to the homogeneous fixed-size design.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, and CR2 variance expansion are unconditional design-based conclusions under group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, fixed \(M\), and bounded potential outcomes; scaled-variance nondegeneracy and predictable-QV stabilization are not used for those conclusions. The centered martingale CLT, CR2 studentized limits, Wald coverage, and sparse studentization conclusion are conditional on the separately named predictable-QV-stable class, with scaled-variance nondegeneracy where division by the asymptotic variance is required. No claim is made that bounded schedules establish predictable-QV stabilization. The sparse result drops \(N_n^2/n\to0\) but trades the comparator's Assumption 1 for that filtration-side premise. The exact software identity is tied to the stated equal-group unweighted intercept-plus-binary-treatment call and versioned package semantics. The impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\), holds on additive no-interference schedules, and therefore transfers upward to arbitrary composition interference; its Rademacher priors satisfy predictable-QV stability by a separate construction-specific theorem. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and Rademacher limit gap vanish. No finite-sample CR2 conservativeness or variable-group-size extension is asserted.

The Kneser calculation here is an unconditional exact-variance result; only the downstream Gaussian conclusions use the separate predictable-QV premise.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix one realized data set and suppress the row index \(n\).  The assertion is deterministic conditional on this realization.  By \({\rm def:random\text{-}partition\text{-}design}\), every realized group has exactly \(M\) units.  For a group \(g\) assigned arm \(z\in\{0,1\}\), let \(y_g\in\mathbb R^M\) collect its individual observed outcomes, let \(\mathbf 1_M\) be the \(M\)-vector of ones, and define
\[
 H_g:=M^{-1}\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}y_g=H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ng},
 \qquad
 x_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1\\ z\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 X_g:=\mathbf 1_Mx_z^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Write \(G_z:=G_{zn}\), so \(G_1=G_{1n}\) and \(G_0=G_{0n}\), and let \(X\) be the matrix obtained by stacking the \(X_g\)'s.  Both treatment values occur because \(G_1,G_0\ge2\); hence the two columns of \(X\) are linearly independent, so \(X\) has rank two.  Since \(M\ge2\), in particular \(M>0\).  Direct multiplication and inversion therefore give
\[
 X^{\mathsf T}X
 =M\begin{pmatrix}G_0+G_1&G_1\\G_1&G_1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B:=(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}
 =\frac1M\begin{pmatrix}
 G_0^{-1}&-G_0^{-1}\\
 -G_0^{-1}&G_0^{-1}+G_1^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The determinant inverted in (2) is \(M^2G_0G_1>0\).  If \(c=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\) selects the treatment coordinate, (2) yields
\[
 c^{\mathsf T}Bx_1=\frac1{MG_1},
 \qquad
 c^{\mathsf T}Bx_0=-\frac1{MG_0}.
 \tag{3}
\]

The cited software contract \({\rm lem:clubsandwich\text{-}cr2\text{-}software\text{-}contract}\), together with the cited \({\tt lm}\)-bread contract \({\rm lem:sandwich\text{-}lm\text{-}bread\text{-}contract}\), says that the returned matrix is
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{CR2}}
 =B\sum_gX_g^{\mathsf T}A_ge_ge_g^{\mathsf T}A_g^{\mathsf T}X_gB,
 \qquad
 A_g=\left(I_M-X_gBX_g^{\mathsf T}\right)^{-1/2},
 \tag{4}
\]
provided the matrices inside the inverse square roots are positive definite.  Here \(e_g=y_g-X_g\widehat\beta\) is the ordinary-least-squares residual block.  To verify the required positivity rather than assume it, set
\[
 P_M:=M^{-1}\mathbf 1_M\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For a group in arm \(z\), (1)--(2) give
\[
 X_gBX_g^{\mathsf T}
 =\mathbf 1_M(x_z^{\mathsf T}Bx_z)\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}
 =G_z^{-1}P_M.
 \tag{5}
\]
The matrix \(P_M\) is the orthogonal projection onto the span of \(\mathbf 1_M\).  Thus \(I_M-G_z^{-1}P_M\) has eigenvalue \(1-G_z^{-1}>0\) on that span, because \(G_z\ge2\), and eigenvalue \(1\) on its orthogonal complement.  This proves the positivity required in (4).  Spectral calculus applied to (5) then gives
\[
 A_g=(I_M-P_M)+a_zP_M,
 \qquad
 a_z:=\left(1-\frac1{G_z}\right)^{-1/2}
 =\sqrt{\frac{G_z}{G_z-1}}.
 \tag{6}
\]

Using (2) in \(\widehat\beta=BX^{\mathsf T}y\), and using equal group size to replace each group total by \(MH_g\), gives
\[
 \widehat\beta
 =\begin{pmatrix}\bar H_0\\ \bar H_1-\bar H_0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \bar H_z:=G_z^{-1}\sum_{g:Z_{ng}=z}H_g.
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently the mean residual in a group \(g\) assigned arm \(z\) is
\[
 M^{-1}\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}e_g=H_g-\bar H_z=:d_g.
 \tag{8}
\]
Equations (6)--(8) imply that the component of \(e_g\) orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1_M\) contributes nothing to the cluster score and that
\[
 \mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}A_ge_g
 =a_z\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}e_g
 =Ma_zd_g.
 \tag{9}
\]
Combining (1), (3), and (9), the treatment-coordinate adjusted score is
\[
 q_g:=c^{\mathsf T}BX_g^{\mathsf T}A_ge_g
 =\begin{cases}
 a_1d_g/G_1,&Z_{ng}=1,\\
 -a_0d_g/G_0,&Z_{ng}=0.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{10}
\]
Taking the treatment-coordinate entry of (4), substituting (10), then using (6) and \({\rm def:cr2\text{-}statistic}\), yields the equation-by-equation identity
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{CR2}}c
 &=\sum_gq_g^2\\
 &=\sum_{z=0}^1\frac{a_z^2}{G_z^2}
   \sum_{g:Z_{ng}=z}(H_g-\bar H_z)^2\\
 &=\sum_{z=0}^1
   \frac{G_z}{G_z-1}\frac{(G_z-1)s_{z,n}^2}{G_z^2}\\
 &=\frac{s_{1,n}^2}{G_{1n}}+\frac{s_{0,n}^2}{G_{0n}}\\
 &=\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{11}
\]
No randomization, independence, moment, or limiting premise is used after fixing the realized data.  The restrictions \(G_{1n},G_{0n}\ge2\) are used exactly to make the CR2 adjustment in (6) finite and the sample variances in \({\rm def:cr2\text{-}statistic}\) well defined.  Equation (11) proves the claimed exact consumer identity.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \({\tt fit}\) be an unweighted, full-column-rank \({\tt lm}\) fit with \(N_{\rm obs}\) fitted observations, model matrix \(X\), cluster-row blocks \(X_g\), and ordinary-least-squares residual blocks \(e_g\).  Suppose that \(I-X_g(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}X_g^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite for every cluster.  In \({\tt clubSandwich}\) version \(0.7.0\), the call \({\tt vcovCR}({\tt fit},\ {\tt cluster},\ {\tt type}={\tt 'CR2'})\), with \({\tt target}\), \({\tt inverse\_var}\), and \({\tt form}\) omitted, uses the identity working target and returns
\[
 \widetilde B
 \sum_gX_g^{\mathsf T}A_ge_ge_g^{\mathsf T}A_g^{\mathsf T}X_g
 \widetilde B,
 \qquad
 \widetilde B=\frac{{\tt sandwich::bread}({\tt fit})}{N_{\rm obs}},
 \qquad
 A_g=\left\{I-X_g(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}X_g^{\mathsf T}\right\}^{-1/2},
\]
where the inverse square root is the symmetric positive-definite one.

 {\tt sandwich::bread}({\tt fit})=N_{\rm obs}(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}.
\]
